methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $62M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Lydian is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Branko Zugic and Joe Rodden that has raised $62.1M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The peer-median method was not applicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables within the climate tech universe. With zero same-stage, zero adjacent-stage, and zero similar-tier valuation peers meeting the threshold of three datapoints, a sector-wide median would introduce unacceptable noise. Accordingly, the Stage-Progression method was applied as the primary valuation anchor. Using total capital raised ($62.1M) as a baseline proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, this method implies a valuation of $124M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $106M to $143M, centered on $124M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression median. The principal uncertainty is the lack of sufficiently narrow peer comparables in the climate tech sector at this stage, which limits triangulation depth. The valuation is therefore heavily dependent on the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier assumption. Users should monitor emergence of later-stage climate tech financings to validate step-up assumptions.
